name: Elishama
overview: Elishama was a male leader from the tribe of Ephraim who served as the head of his tribe during the census taken in the wilderness. He held a significant leadership role among the Israelites during the Exodus, representing Ephraim in the organization of the camp and the people. His position as head of the tribe highlights his importance in the tribal structure during this formative period.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishama means 'G-d has heard,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:10, conveys a recognition of God's attentive care, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Elishama was the son of Ammihud, establishing a clear paternal link in his family lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elishama's role as the head of the tribe of Ephraim during the census underscores his leadership and responsibility in the covenant community of Israel during the Exodus. His leadership contributed to the orderly organization of the tribes, which was essential for the community's journey and encampment. As a tribal leader, he exemplifies the God-ordained structure that preserved Israel's identity and unity under God's guidance.
